name: Museum St. Johann in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: The Museum St. Johann in Tirol: regional history, alpinism on the Wilder Kaiser, Artothek gallery, and geology of the Kitzbüheler Alpen.
beschreibung:
Overview

The modern Museum St. Johann in Tirol is located in the historic market centre of the vibrant municipality of St. Johann in Tirol (Kitzbühel district) at Dechant-Wieshofer-Straße 2, at an altitude of around 660 metres. Framed by the striking rock massif of the Wilder Kaiser and the Kitzbüheler Horn, this cultural venue, founded in 1993, is housed in the former primary school. Awarded the prestigious Österreichisches Museumsgütesiegel, the building unites under one roof a multifaceted local history and mining museum, the Alpine Museum Wilder Kaiser, and a contemporary art gallery.

Alpine History, Mining Heritage & Art

The museum spans a fascinating arc from the earliest prehistoric settlement traces of the Bronze Age to the modern sports and tourism history of the Leukental. A major focus highlights the heyday of mining at Rerobichl in the 16th and 17th centuries: boasting the deepest mine shaft in the world at the time (the Heilig-Geist-Schacht with a depth of nearly 900 metres), St. Johann was a European centre for copper and silver extraction. Original miners' lamps, surveyor maps, and pit tools document the miners' arduous labour. The absolute highlight for mountaineering enthusiasts is the Alpine Museum: dedicated to the dramatic first ascents of the sheer rock faces of the Wilder Kaiser, the exhibition traces the evolution of rock climbing from the pioneers of the Kaiser north faces to modern extreme mountaineering. Historic ropes, pitons, climbing shoes, and personal estates of legendary alpinists are on display. The integrated gallery presents alternating top-tier art exhibitions by contemporary artists from Tyrol and Central Europe.

Visit & Getting There

The Museum St. Johann in Tirol is open from Tuesday to Saturday from 10:00 to 12:00 and from 16:00 to 18:00 (closed on Sundays, Mondays, and public holidays; seasonal break in May and November). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €5.00, seniors approx. €4.00, children and youths (6 to 15 years) approx. €2.50, young children free; family ticket approx. €11.00. Holders of the regional St. Johann Card receive free admission! Getting there by train: St. Johann in Tirol is an important ÖBB express train stop (Giselabahn); from the railway station it is only about a five-minute walk through the pedestrian zone directly to the museum. By car: via the B178 (Loferer Straße) or B161 directly to St. Johann; parking facilities are available in the town centre (Parkgarage Zentrum or Tiefgarage Post).

Tips

The museum is barrier-free and wheelchair-accessible via an outdoor ramp and a passenger elevator. For children, an interactive museum quiz provides a playful way to explore the exhibition rooms. Combine your museum visit with a stroll across the baroque main square of St. Johann and visit the magnificent deanery church of Maria Himmelfahrt with its ceiling frescoes by Simon Benedikt Faistenberger.
